key_insight: ORCHID connects literature-derived finite-temperature thermodynamic evidence to programmatic CALPHAD refinement for materials discovery.
engineering_relevance: Structured, traceable thermodynamic evidence can help engineers refine phase-stability models and evaluate materials under finite-temperature conditions.
method: Extract literature evidence using tiered agents, thermodynamic rules, expert supervision and explicit validation.
Organize values by thermodynamic state, phase identity, provenance, evidence class and uncertainty; export a qualified subset for ESPEI.
Evaluate MLIP-based phase stability with PhaseForge and refine thermodynamic descriptions using ORCHID evidence through PhaseForge+.
evidence_signal: ORCHID contains 73,542 values from 1,321 papers; blind expert evaluation found 93.8% agreement across 48 diagram fields, while Cu–Zr refinement recovered 9 of 13 invariant temperatures within 2σ and reduced held-out activity error from 5.1 to 1.7 kJ/mol.
watch_item: The approximately 27-minute Cu–Zr refinement excludes preparation of the initial description and fitting datasets, and broader system-level generalization remains to be demonstrated.
paper_title: ORCHID: Connecting Finite-Temperature Thermodynamic Evidence to Computational Materials Discovery
